question: Does direct Tieqin catalog evidence for the Copper/Zhunzhai composite object's Huang seal set, one-volume binding and Raoweng provenance materially identify the currently reviewed 1823 NLC Shiliju manuscript as the same physical object?
answer: THE COMPOUND OBJECT FINGERPRINT IS NOW DIRECTLY CLOSED AT THE TIEQIN CATALOG SURFACE AND MATCHES THE CURRENT NLC 1823 OBJECT AT MULTIPLE INDEPENDENT FEATURES: THE SAME TONGHU/ZHUNZHAI TITLE PAIR, ONE-VOLUME COMPOSITE STRUCTURE, HUANG/RAOWENG PROVENANCE, AND THE THREE-PART COPPER VOLUME-HEAD HUANG SEAL SET 士禮居藏 / 黃印丕烈 / 蕘圃. THIS MAKES SAME-PHYSICAL-OBJECT IDENTITY STRONGLY SUPPORTED, BUT IT IS NOT FORMALLY CLOSED BECAUSE NO UNIQUE LATER OWNERSHIP/CALL-NUMBER MARK HAS YET BEEN DIRECTLY MATCHED AND THE FOURTH LOWER SEAL ON THE NLC REPRODUCTION REMAINS UNADJUDICATED. THE HUANG 原書舊鈔 / 錄副 LAYER AND THE 1827 AIRIJINGLU SOURCE-COPY IDENTITY REMAIN UNRESOLVED.
